description: Add an explicit anti-gibberish / single-language discipline directive to the chatbot system prompt as defense-in-depth. The primary provider is now gemini-3.1-flash-lite (clean output), but the provider chain falls through to fallback models (NVIDIA NIM / Groq / Cerebras) on 429/5xx/timeout, and one of those (mistralai/mistral-nemotron) was empirically producing garbled multilingual gibberish (Korean/Japanese/Spanish characters mixed into Hindi). The directive must instruct the model to answer in ONE language only — Hindi (Devanagari) when the user's lang is 'hi' or the question is in Hindi, otherwise English — never mix scripts or insert characters from other languages (no Korean/Japanese/Chinese/Spanish), stay coherent and factual, and if unsure just present the facts plainly. Thread it through the existing signature buildContextForProvider(provider, data, question, lang) which already receives `lang` ('hi' or 'en' from publicChat.js). This REPLACES/UPGRADES the current single Hindi-append line in buildContextForProvider with a fuller, language-parameterized directive; keep the NO_DEV_INSTRUCTIONS_LINE guardrail intact. Depends on FEAT-001 only insofar as both edit publicData.js; do FEAT-002 after FEAT-001.
steps: In mgmt/server-render/src/lib/publicData.js, define a language-directive builder, e.g. `languageDirective(lang)`, that returns a directive string parameterized by lang. For lang === 'hi': instruct the model to reply ONLY in Hindi using Devanagari script (unless the user clearly wrote in English), in one language, without mixing in words or characters from any other language/script (explicitly: no Korean, Japanese, Chinese, or Spanish characters), keeping the answer coherent, factual and plain, and if unsure to simply present the facts plainly rather than guessing. For lang !== 'hi' (English): instruct the model to reply in clear English in one language only, without inserting characters from other scripts/languages, coherent and factual. Keep the wording concise (a couple of sentences) so it does not eat the char budget.

In buildContextForProvider(provider, data, question, lang): after building `context` (full or summary per dataMode), append `languageDirective(lang)`. Remove the current hard-coded single line `if (lang === 'hi') context += '\nReply in simple Hindi (Devanagari) unless the user writes in English.';` and replace it with the new directive (which covers both the 'hi' and English cases). Do NOT change the dataMode selection logic or the function signature.

Do not disturb NO_DEV_INSTRUCTIONS_LINE (which lives inside each context builder's preamble) — the language directive is appended at the buildContextForProvider layer, in addition to, not instead of, that guardrail.

Add node:test unit tests in mgmt/server-render/test/publicChat.test.mjs (import buildContextForProvider): (a) buildContextForProvider({dataMode:'summary'}, SAMPLE, 'q', 'hi') contains a Hindi/Devanagari-language directive that forbids mixing other scripts (assert on the anti-mixing wording, e.g. mentions Devanagari and forbids other-language characters); (b) buildContextForProvider(..., 'en') contains the English single-language directive and does NOT tell the model to reply in Hindi; (c) the directive text differs by the `lang` argument (parameterized, not static); (d) buildContextForProvider still selects buildFullContext when provider.dataMode === 'full' (assert a full-only marker is present) and summarizePortalData otherwise, i.e. the directive did not break dataMode selection; (e) NO_DEV_INSTRUCTIONS_LINE is still present in the produced context for both langs.
Run `npm test` and confirm all tests pass with 0 failures.
acceptance_criteria: `cd mgmt/server-render && npm test` passes with 0 failures.

buildContextForProvider(provider, data, question, 'hi') appends a directive telling the model to answer only in Hindi (Devanagari), in a single language, and to NOT mix in characters from other languages/scripts.
buildContextForProvider(provider, data, question, 'en') appends the English single-language directive and does not instruct a Hindi reply.
The directive is parameterized by `lang` (the 'hi' and 'en' outputs differ).
dataMode selection still works: provider.dataMode === 'full' still routes to buildFullContext; anything else to summarizePortalData.
NO_DEV_INSTRUCTIONS_LINE remains present in the produced context.
The function signature buildContextForProvider(provider, data, question, lang) is unchanged and publicChat.js still compiles/works.
verification: export PATH="/root/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2/bin:$PATH" && cd mgmt/server-render && npm test  (all pass, 0 fail)
Confirm the lang-parameterized assertions would fail if the directive reverted to the old single static Hindi line.
findings: Added languageDirective(lang) helper in mgmt/server-render/src/lib/publicData.js and threaded it through buildContextForProvider (signature unchanged). It replaces the old single hard-coded Hindi line with a fuller, lang-parameterized anti-gibberish / single-language directive: lang==='hi' => reply only in Hindi/Devanagari, one language, no Korean/Japanese/Chinese/Spanish characters; else => English single-language equivalent. NO_DEV_INSTRUCTIONS_LINE guardrail and dataMode (full vs summary) selection untouched. Updated the pre-existing 'routing: dataMode=full' and 'routing: lang=hi' tests (the 'en' path now always appends the directive, and the Hindi text changed from 'Reply in simple Hindi' to 'Reply ONLY in simple Hindi ... Devanagari'), and added 5 new node:test cases covering the hi anti-mixing directive, en single-language directive (no Hindi), lang parameterization, dataMode selection preservation, and NO_DEV_INSTRUCTIONS_LINE presence. npm test: 217 tests, 217 pass, 0 fail.
